newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Taleban ask world to help displaced Afghans.
newsitem.headline: Taleban ask world to help displaced Afghans.

text.p: The governor of the Taleban-held province of Herat in western Afghanistan said on Wednesday that thousands of displaced Afghans could die unless international relief was forthcoming.

Herat governor Mullah Yar Muhammad told the Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press that 50,000 people had been displaced by fighting in the neighbouring province of Badghis and many of them lacked food or shelter against the harsh winter.
He said the most vulnerable were the people in the remote Bala Murghab area, about 180 km (112 miles) northeast of Herat, where it was not easy to deliver relief supplies.
Muhammad said at least 15 people, mostly children, had already died in Bala Murghab for lack of warm bedding.
The Herat governor appealed to U.N. and other international agencies to make more relief supplies available. "Otherwise, thousands of them may perish," he declared.
The U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) agency said on Tuesday it hoped to airlift supplies to Herat for people fleeing recent fighting in Badghis.
"The harsh winter weather has added a new element of urgency to the situation," said Rupert Colville, a UNHCR spokesman.
The UNHCR has asked the radical Islamic Taleban militia, which captured Herat in September last year, to provide transport planes for the proposed airlift.
"The initial response has been positive," Colville said, but could not say when the operation might start.

He said 700 to 800 Afghans were arriving daily from Badghis in Herat, where three hastily built camps already housed 8,300 people. By Monday night, 1,500 people had moved into one camp that had opened the day before. Hundreds, perhaps thousands, of other people may have found shelter with relatives.
The UNHCR estimates that up to 50,000 Afghans may have fled their homes in Badghis to escape recent fighting between the Taleban and the forces of northern General Abdul Rashid Dostum.
The radical Islamic militia is trying to push east through Badghis into Dostum's northern heartland. A Taleban defeat could make Herat vulnerable to an attack by Dostum and his allies.
U.N. sources say both sides have used planes, tanks and heavy artillery in see-saw battles that have raged along the Murghab river and elsewhere for most of this month.
